title: Kymaean Alpha Stage Interaction & Spatial Grammar 01
source_authority: APPUI Phase 2 Stage/live-production studies preserved in Drive

frozen_static_grammar.stage_thesis: Shared invariant-dark performance place; not dashboard, portrait wall, scene illustration, chat transcript, graph, or tile grid.
frozen_static_grammar.carrier: Characters as volumes of light on a dark floor using cone geometry.
frozen_static_grammar.interaction_hinge: Visible focus/selection feedback concentrates around floor/name relationship; semantic hit target may be larger and visually hidden.

spatial_partition.stage_field: Character presence, current fictional performance/state, listening, materially supported opportunity and relationship salience.
spatial_partition.workspace_frame: Production/Scene/current-situation anchors, creator commands, application status, contextual-inspector host.
spatial_partition.contextual_inspector: Invoked current-task information about selected entity; not permanent Stage chrome.
spatial_partition.deep_surfaces: Causal history, deeper Character inspection, bounded perspective, intervention/consequence/technical explanation when separately authorized.

ensemble: identity/state do not depend on exact position
2-5 is design-stress evidence only, not Product cardinality
frozen_static_grammar.navigation_depth: current performance -> immediate causal context -> deeper causal history -> exact return
frozen_static_grammar.theme: White and Black shell presentations surround the same invariant-dark Stage with identical semantics.
frozen_static_grammar.responsive: Stage/current performance survives first; secondary inspection/context may move from adjacency to overlay or sequence.

drift_prohibitions: motive/emotion/knowledge inferred from intensity or position

source_conflicts_found: Early avatar/orb and scenic/dashboard surfaces are not carried forward where they conflict with later selected cone/social-field authority.
Exact motion suggestions in older prototypes remain scaffolding because timing is explicitly unfrozen.
Take a Seat keeps only the explicit-action/bounded-perspective interaction invariant; exact lifecycle labels and runtime semantics remain Product-gated.
